program.title: Deliver a governed and recoverable institutional repository beta
program.outcome: Meet the lab/project repository promise within an explicitly accepted institutional scope.
program.completion: All six required epics and all conditional epics activated by SITE01.3 pass with retained, source-bound evidence. Q03.3 records a named pilot go/no-go. No production source cutover or implementation completion follows from planning.

definitionOfDone: Deliver the stated behavior, satisfy every acceptance criterion and retain the stated evidence; a failed/not-run criterion remains open.
Use existing scientific acceptance, identity, authority and durable-operation contracts. Preserve unrelated work and exact historical releases.
Exercise relevant positive, negative, concurrency, failure and compatibility scenarios; run the suites appropriate to changed boundaries, not unrelated tests by rote.

Record commands/procedures, actual outcomes, source/artifact/configuration identity and limits. Do not substitute synthetic/provider-mock/automated-accessibility evidence for a required institutional or human result.
A gate is an integration/evidence review, not duplicate implementation work. Epic/program closure requires their gates and a current dependency check.
Scope new implementation to a reviewable change; if discovery makes a leaf too broad, split it into blocking child work before claiming completion.
Institutional tasks record missing information and accountable roles without inventing acceptance or sending unsolicited messages.
Conditional epics require an explicit SITE01.3 scope decision. Deferred does not mean implemented; activate blockers before commencing selected conditional work.

epics.title: Labs, projects and a usable collaboration workspace
epics.outcome: A lab steward and researcher can find, organize and share their projects without internal IDs or database assistance.
acceptance: The organizational contract and migration preserve existing scientific releases and attribution.
Authorized project discovery and collaboration screens work across two labs; unauthorized names/counts and revoked access remain hidden.
The two-lab browser/API/PostgreSQL journey and historical-data migration have retained passing evidence.
epics.ownerRole: Technical lead with relevant acceptance owner

epics.title: Institutional identity and current permissions
epics.outcome: Institutional and approved external identities receive only their current, explicit authority.
acceptance: Membership, stewardship, principal disablement and expiring grants are evaluated consistently at every boundary, including long-running work.
One real institutional identity provider and the chosen browser-session design are qualified; email matching never links identities.
Offboarding, revoked/expired sessions, stale contexts and fixed-release boundaries pass positive and negative tests.
epics.ownerRole: Technical lead with relevant acceptance owner

epics.title: Installable and observable institutional service
epics.outcome: An operator can install, upgrade, monitor and bound a supported service.
acceptance: A versioned artifact installs on a clean host with separate migration/runtime privileges and documented configuration.
Health, diagnostic, audit, resource and alert surfaces support real operator actions without disclosing secrets or private scientific metadata.
Database outage, storage exhaustion, interruption and upgrades preserve accepted state within the supported envelope.
epics.ownerRole: Technical lead with relevant acceptance owner

epics.title: Durable storage, withdrawal and independent recovery
epics.outcome: Loss of the original host does not lose the declared recoverable data or resurrect revoked access and withdrawals.
acceptance: Catalog/blob backups and independently durable current policy/lifecycle history survive the declared failure domains.
Restore remains closed on missing, stale, incomplete or unauthenticated policy evidence and invalidates old sessions, credentials and leases.
Revocation/withdrawal after backup, shared references, integrity damage and total-host-loss recovery have measured results; erasure obligations have an enforced admission boundary.
epics.ownerRole: Technical lead with relevant acceptance owner

epics.title: Complete intake, curation, export and project work

acceptance: Governed creation, approved intake, review/acceptance, retry/cancel and verified export work without direct database edits.
Project tasks, notes, release history and review status are usable and obey data permissions.
Every review/result identifies exact releases; failed or partial operations cannot appear completed or scientifically accepted.

epics.title: Institutional pilot evidence and operator handover
epics.outcome: A named institution can make an evidence-backed decision to run a bounded pilot.

Representative correctness/load evidence, independent access review, actual user/accessibility results and operator-led recovery meet that scope.
A recorded pilot go/no-go distinguishes open blockers from accepted limits; primary-repository migration remains a separate decision.
